title: TANDINATOR Original Starter 128
license_note: Original questions and curated answer matrix. Character names and brands remain their owners' property; no affiliation is implied. No Akinator database was used.
portrayal_policy: Best-known mainstream portrayals. Use UNKNOWN for conflicts, missing knowledge or distinctions that would require niche lore. Appearance uses the named familiar portrayal, not every costume or adaptation.

characters.name: Willy Wonka
characters.notes: Use the best-known mainstream portrayal; isolated spin-offs do not determine answers.

characters.name: Paddington Bear
characters.notes: Brown bear from Peru, best known in London with a blue duffel coat and red hat.

characters.name: Abraham Lincoln
characters.notes: US president, 1809-1865; iconic beard without a moustache.

characters.name: George Washington
characters.notes: US president and military commander; white powdered hairstyle is the familiar portrait image.

characters.name: Albert Einstein
characters.notes: Physicist; public scientific career belongs mainly to the 20th century. White hair is the familiar later-life image.

characters.name: Isaac Newton
characters.notes: English scientist and mathematician; no claim is made about everyday clothing colors.

characters.name: Marie Curie
characters.notes: Polish-born scientist working in France. Scientific activity began in the 1800s and continued in the 1900s.

characters.name: Ada Lovelace
characters.notes: British mathematician associated with early computing; not credited here with physically building a machine.

characters.name: Leonardo da Vinci
characters.notes: Italian Renaissance artist and inventor; later-life bearded portrait is the reference.

characters.name: Cleopatra
characters.notes: Cleopatra VII of ancient Egypt; familiar dark-haired depiction is cultural iconography rather than a verified portrait.

characters.name: Joan of Arc
characters.notes: French historical military figure; hair details are not confidently standardized.

characters.name: Nelson Mandela
characters.notes: South African president and anti-apartheid leader. No current-life status question is used.

characters.name: Mahatma Gandhi
characters.notes: Indian independence leader; not classified as a government officeholder. Public activism began in the 1890s.

characters.name: Amelia Earhart
characters.notes: American aviation pioneer; ordinary aircraft do not make the supernatural flight question yes.

characters.name: Elvis Presley
characters.notes: Recognizable later-career white stage jumpsuits; otherwise costume colors vary.

characters.name: Michael Jackson
characters.notes: Signature performance glove and stage imagery; no sensitive medical or appearance speculation.

characters.name: Dolly Parton
characters.notes: Country singer, songwriter, instrumentalist and businesswoman; outfits vary.

characters.name: Freddie Mercury
characters.notes: Queen frontman; the moustached 1980s stage appearance is the reference.

characters.name: Beyonce
characters.notes: Stage performer; hairstyle and hair color vary, so no fixed color is asserted.

characters.name: Mr. T
characters.notes: Actor and television personality; gold jewelry and distinctive hair/beard are recognizable. Real-world strength is not superhuman.

characters.name: Hulk Hogan
characters.notes: Professional wrestler; blond handlebar moustache and yellow/red ring attire are iconic. No superhuman ability is asserted.

characters.name: Muhammad Ali
characters.notes: Boxer and civil-rights figure. Boxing counts as trained hand-to-hand combat in final corrections.

characters.name: Serena Williams
characters.notes: Tennis champion; no fixed playing-outfit color is asserted.

characters.name: Colonel Sanders
characters.notes: Harland Sanders, KFC founder and brand figure; white suit and facial hair are the reference.
